note: Numbers are copied from the named table/section of each paper. A headline without its baseline is E3 and cannot promote.

mechanisms.title: ReAct interleaved thought-action loop
mechanisms.why_relevant: The default tool-using agent loop this program already meets in the wild; used only as the known-existing-implementation control.
mechanisms.spec_clarity: Algorithm is fully specified: Thought / Action / Observation loop with a small action space (Search, Lookup, Finish) and in-context trajectories.

paper.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
paper.authors: Yao, Zhao, Yu, Du, Shafran, Narasimhan, Cao
paper.section_or_figure: Table 3 (ALFWorld task-specific success rates) and the ALFWorld subsection of Experiments

effect_size.metric: ALFWorld average success rate percent, best-of-6 greedy trials

baseline.name: BUTLER best-of-8 (Shridhar et al. 2020b, Table 4 of that paper, cited in ReAct Table 3)

mechanisms.title: Two-expert debate judged by a weaker non-expert
mechanisms.why_relevant: A specified deliberation protocol for this program's council/verifier path: two experts argue opposite answers; a weaker judge picks. Consultancy is the named non-adversarial baseline.
mechanisms.spec_clarity: Protocol 2.1 specifies debate, interactive debate, and consultancy: N simultaneous rounds, shared transcript, judge chooses; consultancy is one expert plus probing judge.

paper.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
paper.authors: Khan, Hughes, Valentine, Ruis, Sachan, Radhakrishnan, Grefenstette, Bowman, Rocktaschel, Perez
paper.section_or_figure: Abstract and the weak-judge result paragraph (human 88% / LLM 76% vs naive 60% / 48%; consultancy 78% / 54%)

effect_size.metric: non-expert human judge accuracy on QuALITY with the most persuasive debaters

baseline.name: naive human baseline (no expert arguments) 60%; consultancy human judges 78% is the non-adversarial protocol baseline

mechanisms.title: Chain-of-Verification factor+revise
mechanisms.why_relevant: A four-step self-deliberation protocol (draft, plan checks, answer checks independently, revise) that is specified enough to implement as a verifier stage.
mechanisms.spec_clarity: Section 3 names four steps; the factor+revise variant answers verification questions in isolated prompts and then cross-checks before the final rewrite.

paper.title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
paper.authors: Dhuliawala, Komeili, Xu, Raileanu, Li, Celikyilmaz, Weston
paper.section_or_figure: Table 1 Wikidata precision; Table 3 longform FactScore for factor+revise

secondary_effect.metric: biography FactScore, CoVe factor+revise vs few-shot (Table 3)

mechanisms.title: Prover-Verifier Games for output legibility
mechanisms.why_relevant: Relevant to verifier/legibility training, but this row is the E3 control: a headline without a paired numeric baseline extracted from a named table.
mechanisms.spec_clarity: Training loop is specified (helpful prover, sneaky prover, small verifier) after Anil et al. 2021; this row deliberately omits a numeric effect/baseline pair.

paper.title: Prover-Verifier Games improve legibility of LLM outputs
paper.authors: Kirchner, Chen, Edwards, Leike, McAleese, Burda
paper.section_or_figure: Abstract / Figure 1 qualitative trade-off (not a copied table cell)
paper.headline_only: Checkability training retains high legibility with accuracy between initialization and a correctness-only PPO baseline (legibility tax). No numeric pair copied from a table into this row.
